The 49 fathom-only: 46 `super(...)` (upstream tags no super), 2 a name upstream's locals.scm reads as a local of a `def self.x` it does not scope (singleton_method and module are no scopes there, so `engines` and `body` leak to the scope around), and 1 the `call` of a `def block.each` paired with the method around it. call_recall was .6622 before constants became call targets (and the same dialect held sym_recall .9451, L1 good, before constants, attr_* names, aliases and define_method became definitions).

changes to the previous ruby dialect (same SourceKinds kept, every symbol it listed still emitted, TestRubyDialectKeepsLegacySymbols): new are RubyConstant (a container, so `Outer::CONST` and the methods of a Struct.new block qualify), RubyProperty (attr_accessor, attr_reader and attr_writer names, qualified `Owner.name`), RubyAlias (`alias` and `alias_method`), RubyMethod for define_method with a literal name, RubyClass and RubyModule for `Name = Class.new` and `Module.new` (and bound to a local), a constant reference as a call target, and .rake, .ru and Rakefile as Ruby; since LB-F254 a bare identifier is a call unless a local binds it (a parameter, an assignment, a rescue variable, a for target or a pattern binding in its def, class, module or file, or one a block or lambda around it sees). Not emitted, on purpose: `def obj.x` on a local (no owner to qualify it), `attr :x`, an operator as a call, and the assignments ctags does not read either (`A, B = 1, 2`, `X ||= 1`, `A::B = 1`).

file_edge_precision and file_edge_recall measured against an import dump's (file, imported file) pairs, there being no SCIP index: the truth is what each file's import statements name, not the files its references reach as a SCIP index's cross-file edges are, so a file reached without an import of its own (a file another one required, an autoloaded constant) is outside the truth and a resolved edge to it counts against precision, while a file imported and never referenced is in it (LB-F57)
